observation: The Melian Dialogue is compared with Nuer feud settlement to distinguish emotion, action, organisation, and scale.
Jebel Sahaba's healed and unhealed projectile injuries support recurrent violence, while Nataruk's body scatter supports a more bounded but debated event.
The Stele of the Vultures joins divine sanction, irrigation boundaries, army formation, and territorial administration; Mohenjo-daro checks overconfident massacre inference.
Behistun classifies rival claimants as liars and rebels, while Assyrian deportation records turn conquered households into movable labour.
Cajamarca and Tenochtitlan show that ruler capture worked differently amid Inca succession conflict and the Mexica system of tributary rivalries and alliances.
The Bayeux Tapestry and Domesday connect dynastic conquest to land reassignment, while Jerusalem's chroniclers connect penitential vows to massacre and later government.
Temujin converts remembered personal loyalty into offices and redistributed households; Novgorod's census then shows conquest becoming recurring tribute.
The Code Noir places baptism, family, sale, and mutilation in one legal order, and the Zong litigation converts killings into an insurance dispute challenged by Equiano.
The devşirme links village selection to training, payroll, and firearms, whereas Magdeburg shows an army converting a captured city's goods into supply and reward.
The October march pressures living political authorities and forces their relocation, while the September prison killings target people already classified and confined.
Casement follows Congo rubber coercion from quotas through agents and the Force Publique; Maji Maji shows cotton demands, religious mobilisation, machine-gun repression, and famine.
The Somme's shells depend on factories, trains, and registers, while Ottoman deportation orders direct the same administrative reach toward Armenian civilians.
Wannsee coordinates ministries around an existing extermination policy, and the Sonderkommando photographs document killing from a coerced prisoner's obstructed viewpoint.
Cuban missile correspondence exposes deterrence's dependence on signalling and dispersed command, while the Briggs Plan couples resettlement, food control, intelligence, and reform.
Taiping demographic deficits cannot cleanly separate battle, famine, migration, and missing births; Clarkson's evidence shows records being assembled to redirect state power against the slave trade.
